original_text:
Virus Structure¨Range from 10-400nm in size¨Categorized by 1) shape, 2) genetic material, & 3) presence /absence of outer envelope
¨All Viruses contain same basic anatomy otherwise:¤Outer capsid made of protein complexes¤Inner core of nucleic acid –3 to 100’s of genes.¨Viruses with no envelope said to be “Naked”¨Enveloped viruses covered in outer coating made of cell plasma membrane.
explanation: Viruses range in size from 10 to 400 nm. They are categorized based on three criteria: shape, genetic material, and the presence or absence of an outer envelope. All viruses possess a common basic anatomy consisting of an outer protein capsid (made of protein complexes) and an inner core of nucleic acid, which contains between 3 to hundreds of genes. Viruses that lack an outer envelope are termed 'naked' viruses. Enveloped viruses feature an outer coating made of cell plasma membrane acquired from the host cell.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three criteria used to categorize viruses?
opts: Presence or absence of an outer envelope
questions.exp: Viruses are categorized by shape, genetic material, and the presence/absence of an outer envelope. Host cell metabolism is not one of the criteria.

questions.q: What is the outer coating of an enveloped virus composed of?
opts: Pure lipid droplets synthesized by the capsid
questions.exp: The notes state that enveloped viruses are covered in an outer coating made of cell plasma membrane.

questions.q: What is the genetic capacity of a virus's inner core of nucleic acid?
questions.exp: The notes specify that the inner core of nucleic acid has '3 to 100’s of genes'.
